messages:
emily: FYI — caught a nasty duplicate-create from one of our Python async sample apps. Repro steps: transient 502, then socket reset, client retried and replayed JSON body -> two resources.

sam: oh no. any logs? :grimacing:

emily: pasted below. The client enqueued a retry after the reset and didn't detect the original might have been accepted.

emily: truncated logs:
```
2026-03-02T10:02:13Z INFO POST /v1/items -> 502 Bad Gateway
2026-03-02T10:02:13Z ERROR write: connection reset by peer
2026-03-02T10:02:13Z INFO retry scheduled attempt=1 delay=200ms
2026-03-02T10:02:13Z INFO retry dispatching request
2026-03-02T10:02:13Z INFO 201 Created id=item_7X
```
```
2026-03-02T10:02:14Z WARN original request may have been accepted; detected duplicate ids: item_7X, item_7Y
```

emily: sample code (very minimal):
```
client = RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'], timeout=8)
await client.post('/v1/items', json={'name': 'demo-item'})
```

emily: note: demo didn't set Idempotency-Key.

ritika: I thought our retry semantics avoid replay for non-idempotent ops by default?

andrew: historically we stored bodies so retries could replay for convenience. We attempted to special-case streaming bodies, but for small JSON we treat them as replayable. The missing piece is verifying whether the socket write actually completed upstream before deciding to replay.

sam: so if the server wrote an ack then reset, client thinks failure and resends -> duplicate create.

emily: exactly — embarrassing during a live customer demo.

andrew: short-term mitigation: update sample apps to set an Idempotency-Key header and add a comment explaining importance for create endpoints. Also increase client timeout in sample to reduce premature retries on flaky networks.

ritika: longer-term fix idea: change default to "do not replay non-idempotent POSTs unless user opt-in or provides Idempotency-Key". That could be a breaking behavioral change.

andrew: agreed. Suggest we add a runtime guard: if method is POST and no Idempotency-Key, mark as non-replayable and log a dev-warning when retry attempted. Also emit a telemetry metric (retry_blocked_non_idempotent).

sam: I like the safe default. We should also ship a migration note and a flag to preserve old behavior for existing users for one release.

emily: can we detect partial socket writes? Maybe the transport can surface whether write finished before reset. If we can detect that, we could avoid blind replays.

andrew: technically possible but tricky across transports (asyncio, trio). Better to implement the safer default first and then explore partial-write detection as an enhancement.

ritika: tests: add an integration that simulates 502 + connection reset mid-send and assert no duplicate create when Idempotency-Key absent. Also a test that ensures users who set Idempotency-Key still get retry behavior.

andrew: I'll draft a PR with three pieces: runtime non-replay guard, telemetry counter, and integration test harness using our flaky-server. ETA 48-72h. Will add a client flag like replay_policy = 'safe'|'legacy' behind a deprecation note.

sam: I'll update examples in the quickstart and sample-app repo to include Idempotency-Key usage and a short paragraph in onboarding docs. ETA 24h.

emily: action items:
- andrew: PR for non-replayable POST default + telemetry + integration test (ETA 3d)
- sam: sample-app + quickstart updates to show Idempotency-Key (ETA 1d)
- ritika: doc blurb for SDK retry semantics and migration note (ETA 1d)
- emily: file a support ticket for the customer demo and include mitigation steps (ETA today)

ci-bot: queued CI for PR #855 (sdk-python) :github:

andrew: follow-up thought: introduce a helper util for sample apps that sets a UUID Idempotency-Key automatically for demos. That reduces friction while keeping safe defaults.

sam: good idea; we can add that helper to the quickstart snippets.

emily: thanks all — please ping this thread when PR lands so I can confirm sample-app fix.

ci-bot: PR #855 passed unit tests; integration queued.
